businessModelCanvas.description: The Business Model Canvas (BMC) is a strategic management tool that provides a visual framework for developing, describing, and analyzing business models. The expanded SDG-adapted version consists of 11 interconnected building blocks, including Social and Environmental Cost and Social and Environmental Benefit.

blocks.name: Customer Segments
blocks.description: Defines the different groups of people or organizations an enterprise aims to reach and serve. Customers comprise the heart of any business model.
keyQuestions: For whom are we creating value?
Who are our most important customers?
What are the customer archetypes?
relationships: Value Propositions are designed for specific Customer Segments
Channels deliver value to Customer Segments
Customer Relationships are established with each segment

blocks.name: Value Propositions
blocks.description: Describes the bundle of products and services that create value for a specific Customer Segment. It solves a customer problem or satisfies a need.
keyQuestions: What value do we deliver to the customer?
Which customer needs are we satisfying?
What bundles of products/services are we offering?
relationships: Value Propositions serve specific Customer Segments
Key Activities and Resources create Value Propositions

blocks.name: Channels
blocks.description: Describes how a company communicates with and reaches its Customer Segments to deliver a Value Proposition. Channels serve several functions: awareness, evaluation, purchase, delivery, and after-sales.
keyQuestions: Through which channels do our customers want to be reached?
How do we reach them now?
Which channels work best and are most cost-efficient?
examples: Direct: Sales force, Web sales, Own stores
relationships: Channels deliver Value Propositions to Customer Segments

blocks.name: Customer Relationships
blocks.description: Describes the types of relationships a company establishes with specific Customer Segments. Motivations: customer acquisition, customer retention, boosting sales.
keyQuestions: What type of relationship does each segment expect?
Which ones have we established?
How costly are they?
relationships: Customer Relationships are established with each Customer Segment

blocks.name: Revenue Streams
blocks.description: Represents the cash a company generates from each Customer Segment. Revenue Streams can involve one-time transactions or recurring revenues.
keyQuestions: For what value are customers willing to pay?
What are they currently paying for?
How would they prefer to pay?
relationships: Revenue Streams are generated from Customer Segments through Value Propositions

blocks.name: Key Resources
blocks.description: Describes the most important assets required to make a business model work. They allow an enterprise to create and offer value, reach markets, and earn revenues.
keyQuestions: What key resources do our value propositions require?
Our distribution channels?
Customer relationships?
relationships: Key Resources enable creation of Value Propositions, maintenance of Customer Relationships, and operation of Channels

blocks.name: Key Activities
blocks.description: Describes the most important things a company must do to make its business model work. These are the critical actions for creating Value Propositions.
keyQuestions: What key activities do our value propositions require?
Our distribution channels?
Revenue streams?
relationships: Key Activities use Key Resources to create Value Propositions and maintain operations

blocks.name: Key Partnerships
blocks.description: Describes the network of suppliers and partners that make the business model work. Companies forge partnerships to optimize, reduce risk, or acquire resources.
keyQuestions: Who are our key partners and suppliers?
Which key resources are we acquiring from partners?
Which key activities do partners perform?
relationships: Key Partnerships provide Key Resources or perform Key Activities

blocks.name: Cost Structure
blocks.description: Describes all costs incurred to operate a business model. Costs can be cost-driven (minimize costs) or value-driven (premium value creation).
keyQuestions: What are the most important costs inherent in our business model?
Which key resources are most expensive?
Which key activities are most expensive?
relationships: Cost Structure is determined by Key Resources, Key Activities, and Key Partnerships

blocks.name: Social and Environmental Cost
blocks.description: Describes the negative social and environmental impacts (externalities) of the business model — emissions, waste, resource depletion, community harm, or health risks.
keyQuestions: What negative social impacts does our business model create?
What environmental harm or resource depletion results from our operations?
Who bears these costs and can they be mitigated?
relationships: Social and Environmental Cost should be weighed against Revenue Streams and Social and Environmental Benefit

blocks.name: Social and Environmental Benefit
blocks.description: Describes the positive social and environmental contributions of the business model — jobs created, access to essential services, carbon reduction, education, or health improvements. Often mapped to UN SDGs.
keyQuestions: What positive outcomes does our business create for society?
What environmental improvements result from our model?
Which SDGs does our business advance?
relationships: Social and Environmental Benefit complements Value Propositions and Revenue Streams

swotAnalysis.description: SWOT Analysis is a strategic planning technique that identifies Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, and Threats. It helps organizations understand internal capabilities and external environment.

strengths.description: Internal positive attributes and resources that support achieving objectives
promptingQuestions: What unique resources do we have?
What do others see as our strengths?
What competitive advantages do we have?

weaknesses.description: Internal factors that detract from the ability to achieve objectives
promptingQuestions: Where do we have fewer resources than others?
What are others likely to see as weaknesses?

opportunities.description: External factors the organization could exploit to its advantage
promptingQuestions: What trends could we take advantage of?
What opportunities are open to us?
What technology changes could benefit us?
What policy/regulatory changes may benefit us?

threats.description: External factors that could cause trouble for the organization
promptingQuestions: Are quality standards or specifications changing?
Is changing technology threatening our position?

scoringCriteria.impact: Rate 1-5 how significantly this factor affects business outcomes
scoringCriteria.likelihood: Rate 1-5 the probability of this factor materializing
scoringCriteria.timeframe: Near-term (< 1 year), Medium (1-3 years), Long-term (3+ years)

portersFiveForces.description: Porter's Five Forces is a framework for analyzing competitive forces within an industry to determine the intensity of competition and profitability potential.

forces.name: Threat of New Entrants
forces.description: How easy or difficult it is for new competitors to enter the industry

forces.name: Bargaining Power of Suppliers
forces.description: How much pressure suppliers can place on a business

forces.name: Bargaining Power of Buyers
forces.description: How much pressure customers can place on a business

forces.name: Threat of Substitutes
forces.description: How easily customers can find alternative products or services

forces.name: Industry Rivalry
forces.description: The intensity of competition among existing competitors

valuePropositionCanvas.description: The Value Proposition Canvas helps ensure that a product or service is positioned around what the customer values and needs.

customerProfile.jobs: Tasks customers are trying to perform, problems they're trying to solve, or needs they want to satisfy
customerProfile.pains: Negative outcomes, risks, and obstacles related to customer jobs

valueMap.products: Products and services the value proposition is built around
valueMap.painRelievers: How products and services alleviate customer pains
valueMap.gainCreators: How products and services create customer gains

leanCanvas.description: The Lean Canvas is a 1-page business plan template adapted from the Business Model Canvas. It focuses on problems, solutions, and key metrics for startups.
elements: Unfair Advantage (Something that cannot be easily copied)
Cost Structure (Customer acquisition costs, distribution costs, hosting, people)
Revenue Streams (Revenue model, lifetime value, revenue, gross margin)

businessModelPatterns.description: Common business model patterns that can be combined and adapted

patterns.name: Freemium
patterns.description: Basic service is free; premium features require payment
patterns.bestFor: Digital products with low marginal costs and network effects

patterns.name: Subscription
patterns.description: Recurring revenue through periodic payments for continued access
patterns.bestFor: Services with ongoing value delivery and predictable costs

patterns.name: Marketplace/Platform
patterns.description: Connect buyers and sellers, taking a fee for facilitating transactions
patterns.bestFor: Industries with fragmented supply and demand

patterns.name: Razor and Blades
patterns.description: Sell the base product cheaply, profit from consumables/add-ons

patterns.name: Direct-to-Consumer (D2C)
patterns.description: Sell directly to end consumers, bypassing traditional retail
patterns.bestFor: Brands wanting control over customer experience and data

patterns.name: Pay-as-you-go
patterns.description: Customers pay based on actual usage rather than a fixed fee
patterns.bestFor: Variable-demand services where usage varies significantly

patterns.name: Social Enterprise
patterns.description: Business model that prioritizes social/environmental impact alongside financial sustainability

dilemmaTriangle.description: The Dilemma Triangle (Triple Bottom Line) framework examines tensions between People, Planet, and Prosperity (Profit). Sustainable businesses must balance all three dimensions.

drivers.name: People
drivers.description: Social equity, fair labor practices, community development, human rights, stakeholder well-being

drivers.name: Planet
drivers.description: Environmental sustainability, resource conservation, emissions reduction, biodiversity, circular economy

drivers.name: Prosperity
drivers.description: Economic viability, profitability, long-term growth, financial inclusion, shared value creation
